title: The fading account's new fleet contact asks for a quote in the website chat; two days to a person's first reply
demonstrates: A hand-over that nobody takes. The assistant will not price fleet work, takes a number and hands over at 10:14 on Tuesday. The lead advisor reads it at 16:02 and passes it on in a private note; the newcomer answers 'on it' in another note. A note answers nobody: the customer's follow-up on Wednesday gets a draft that sits. Thursday at 10:41 the newcomer sends that draft as it was, promises 'today', answers one of her two questions, and the quote arrives at 16:47. The assistant's last draft answers the question he skipped, and he sends it untouched.

timeline.text: Hello, this is Erin Castillo with Sourwood Catering. We have an account with your East Main shop.

I need an itemized quote on two of our vehicles before I schedule anything. SC-4 (the 2019 ProMaster): front brakes, pads and rotors. You quoted its brakes about a month ago and we did not go ahead. SC-9 (the 2017 box truck): a new battery. Parts and labor separate, please. Our owner signs off on these Friday morning.

Hello Erin, I'm the assistant for Brennan Auto Care. I can't prepare a quote for specific fleet vehicles from here, and I don't want to give you list prices that may not match your account. I'll pass your request to the service advisors at East Main so they can send an itemized quote. What's the best phone number for you?
Thank you, Erin. Your request is with the team now, and somebody will get back to you as soon as possible.

why: Erin stays in full sentences and her lines get shorter: an introduction, 'Following up', 'I do need it today', 'Received, thank you.' Nobody is rude.
Travis writes to a colleague, not to the customer, slowly and with the typos left in.
Caleb: 'should', an exclamation mark on a late answer, the first of two questions, and two drafts sent untouched, the second of which does his job for him.
For S1 an agent finds here: the hand-off instant, the two notes, the first human line two days later.
